EXPECTED — 01-note-single.txt
=============================
The smallest useful unit: one dictated sentence pair, two claims.

SHOULD PRODUCE (3-4 facts, all pending):
  kb:lumenpath        rdfs:label       "Lumenpath"            [after repair]
  kb:lumenpath        kpred:is-a       kb:enterprise-cad
  kb:enterprise-cad   kpred:used-by    kb:architecture-studio
  kb:enterprise-cad   kpred:purpose    "manage drawings and models"

MUST NOT PRODUCE:
  kb:lumen-path-is-an-enterprise-cad-platform
      A whole sentence as one entity slug. rdf/triple-shape.ts
      (looksLikeProposition) rejects this at the door — verified 2026-09-02 —
      so its appearance is a REGRESSION in that guard, not a model failure.

KNOWN-BROKEN, do not record as a new finding:
  · "Lumen path" is very unlikely to be repaired to "Lumenpath" on a FRESH
    graph. vocabulary-repair matches against names the graph ALREADY HAS, so
    with nothing to match it cannot fire. This is correct behaviour and the
    reason note 02 seeds the vocabulary first.
  · "cad" will not be capitalised to CAD. Nothing in the pipeline knows the
    acronym, and the homophone is real English, so no rule catches it. This is
    the "enterprise dam" case exactly.
  · No rdf:type will be proposed. Measured 0 of 16 on the real corpus — no
    built-in type carries the predicates a dictated note produces (F149).
  · No skos:broader. Extraction emits none; co-hyponym inference is not wired
    into the app, only into the offline chain harness.

WHAT TO JUDGE: are the two claims separated into distinct facts with a real
subject, or collapsed into one node? That is the only question this file asks.
